systems.name: Te Papa's maramataka activity sequence
systems.description: The planting, fishing and gathering guidance Te Papa gives night by night through the maramataka, numbered here in the order the page lists it.
systems.uncertainty: The numbers are the order of Te Papa's page, not established night numbers: several of the page's positions are fractional or repeated (2.5, 7.8, a second 12). Night names are given only where the page's text names them. Iwi differ in names, number and order. Do not use this as a conversion table.

systems.name: Religious lunar calendar
systems.description: A lunar reckoning used for temple festivals alongside the civil calendar.
systems.month_rule: One Egyptian reckoning began the month on the day the old Moon could no longer be seen.
systems.uncertainty: Egyptian lunar months could begin by different conventions (temple service months among them), so these days are not placed on modern dates.

systems.name: Civil calendar
systems.year_rule: 12 months of 30 days, plus 5 extra days: 365 days.
systems.sky_and_seasons: Three seasons: Akhet (inundation), Peret (emergence) and Shemu (harvest).
systems.uncertainty: Not placed on modern dates: a 365-day year drifts against the seasons, and where it stood in a given year needs a specified historical convention.

systems.name: Athenian lunar month
systems.description: The civic and religious month of Athens, with named days at its start and end.
systems.month_rule: The month began with the Noumenia; Athens fixed the start by civic convention.
systems.uncertainty: Month starts followed civic convention, and modern reconstructed calendars vary, so these days are not placed on modern dates.

systems.name: Four-day market week
systems.description: Four named market days, Eke, Orie, Afọ and Nkwọ, repeating in order. The day names also appear in personal names.
systems.uncertainty: No universal Gregorian anchor: which day is Eke today differs between communities, so the cycle is not placed on the calendar.

systems.name: Five-day week recorded by A. B. Ellis
systems.description: A five-day week recorded in a nineteenth-century account, each day after the first sacred to an orisha.
systems.uncertainty: This historical account conflicts with contemporary descriptions of a four-day Yoruba week. It is kept as its own variant, not as the Yoruba calendar, and is not placed on dates until a local lineage and starting point are established.

cycles.name: Market week
cycles.regional_note: The order Eke, Orie, Afọ, Nkwọ is documented; the day on which a given community's Eke falls varies.

cycles.name: Five-day week (Ellis)
cycles.regional_note: Contemporary accounts describe a four-day week instead; this five-day account is a separate historical variant.
